question_text: Which type of communication is employed in mobile phones?

mark_split.label: Why space wave is the type used

Physics hand-checked: mobile phones use wireless communication by space-wave (line-of-sight) propagation in a cellular network; their frequencies are far above 30 MHz, so the waves pass through the ionosphere and the signal must travel in a straight line between the phone and a nearby base-station tower.

recall_prompt: Say which type of communication mobile phones use, and why that type and not sky wave.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Wireless — space wave
lines: as part of a cellular network.
steps.margin_note: First mark. The words space wave; line of sight makes the answer complete.
steps.why: The question asks for the TYPE of communication, and the type has a name: space-wave, also called line-of-sight, propagation — the wave travels straight from the phone to a nearby tower, and the network of towers (cells) carries it onward.
common_mistakes: Writing sky wave. Mobile-phone frequencies are not reflected by the ionosphere, so sky wave cannot carry them.
Writing only 'wireless'. Wireless is the family; the type asked for is space wave (line of sight).

recall.must_convey: That mobile phones use wireless communication by space-wave, line-of-sight propagation in a cellular network.
accept: wireless, space wave, in a cellular network
reject: the waves pass through the ionosphere

steps.memory_tip: Phone to tower in a straight line — the name space wave means the wave crosses the space between them directly.

lines.text: Mobile phones: space wave (line of sight)

steps.margin_note: Second mark. Above 30 MHz the ionosphere does not reflect — so line of sight is the only way.
steps.why: The reason is the same 30 MHz limit that defines sky wave: above it the ionosphere lets the wave through, so long hops off the ionosphere are impossible and the signal must go straight to a nearby receiver — which is why the network needs many towers close together.
common_mistakes: Saying the ionosphere reflects mobile signals. Above about 30 MHz it does not — the wave passes through.
Saying one tall tower serves a whole state. Line of sight is short-range, so the cellular network uses many towers, each covering one small cell.

recall.must_convey: That mobile-phone frequencies are above 30 MHz, pass through the ionosphere, and so must travel line of sight to a nearby tower.
accept: the ionosphere does not reflect them
the signal goes straight to a nearby tower
reject: space wave in a cellular network

steps.memory_tip: Sky wave stops at about 30 MHz; mobile phones are far above it, so their signals must go straight to a nearby tower.

insider_note: First mark: the named type, space wave (line of sight). Second: the 30 MHz reason — the ionosphere passes these frequencies, so the wave must go straight to a nearby tower.
